INFR11269 Coursework: submission requirements 
Assessment components 
Component   Submission   Contribution to the 
coursework mark 
Group report, supported by a video   One submission per group   70% 
Individual review   One review of one assigned submission 
per student   30% 
ASR and RAG are assessed together as one piece of systems work. They do not have separate mark 
allocations. The video supports assessment of the group report and has no separate mark. Group 
members receive the same group - report mark; each student receives their own individual - review 
mark. 
Use the submission links and deadlines published on Learn.   If there are two members in the group, 
both   members should upload the same report pdf , as the system will randomly select one of them for 
marking and   review. 
Written report 
Submit a PDF using the supplied coursework report template. The main body must be no longer than 
six pages . References, optional appendices and the final declaration/student - information page are 
outside this limit. Keep the supplied style, page geometry and anonymous review mode. 
The report should explain: 
•   The system context, a precise question and why it matters. 
•   The baseline, the technical work you completed and the reasons for your design choices. 
•   How you evaluated the work, including comparison conditions, metrics and relevant configuration. 
•   Results for an appropriate quality or correctness measure and an appropriate systems - cost 
measure. 
•   What the results support, why the observed behaviour occurs, and the limitations of the 
investigation. 
Explain your ASR work and RAG investigation in a coherent account of the system. Distinguish 
supplied components from your own contributions.   Focus on components you implement.   Focus on 
well - supported claims   instead of numerous shallow ideas . The template's section headings are 
suggestions; organise the report to suit your investigation. 
Make comparisons interpretable: identify the baseline, data split, sample size, relevant settings and 
what changes between runs. State what each timing includes, such as model loading, ASR, retrieval 
or API calls. Where relevant, explain caching, repeated measurements and variability. Label all 
figures and tables with their metrics and units. For answer evaluation, report the judge settings and 
recognise the limits of automated scores. 
Keep essential methods, results and arguments in the main body. Reviewers are not required to read 
appendices. Explain negative results and incomplete work accurately. A well - designed investigation 
does not need to outperform the baseline to earn a strong mark. 
Place the AI - use declaration and student information on   one final page , using the template. Put your 
Group ID, names and UUNs on that page only. Keep all technical content before it: the final page will 
be removed before peer review.

2 
Supporting video 
Submit one video per group, with a   maximum duration of ten minutes : 
Part   Time allocation   Content 
Presentation and 
demonstration   Up to eight minutes   Explain the system, your technical work and key 
findings, and show the system running 
Answers to two questions   Reserve the final two 
minutes 
Answer both questions released by the course team 
one week before the report submission deadline 
A shorter presentation is acceptable; retain the final two - minute section for the questions. Clearly 
introduce each answer as Question 1 or Question 2. 
For the demonstration, show an actual run of your system, its input and its output. Identify the 
configuration and explain what the output demonstrates. If a run is slow, you may shorten waiting 
periods; make any cuts clear. Screenshots or previously recorded metrics can explain results, but 
include a recorded run rather than relying entirely on slides. Make terminal output, figures and other 
on - screen material readable. 
Use the video to explain your design choices, interpret the results and demonstrate your 
understanding. Include the central experimental evidence and conclusions in the written report as well. 
Each group submits a single video; there is no requirement for every member to speak or appear. 
MP4 is recommended. Follow the video upload route and any file - size settings published on Learn. 
Check playback, audio and legibility before submitting. 
For a practical recording, editing and compression workflow using free tools, see the   v ideo production 
guide . 
Anonymity 
Use an anonymous project title in the report and video. Keep your own names, UUNs, email 
addresses and Group IDs out of the report body, appendices, video content and optional code. The 
report's final student - information page is the sole exception. References should use normal scholarly 
citations without wording that identifies you as an author. 
For the video, use a screen recording with narration. Do not include webcam footage, faces, 
introductions by name or identifying credits. Ordinary voice narration is allowed; you do not need to 
alter your voice. Hide account names, personal file paths, browser profiles, notifications and other 
identifying details shown on screen. 
Use neutral filenames such as   report.pdf ,   video.mp4   and   supplementary_code.zip . Avoid identifying 
author metadata in the PDF or video. If you submit code, remove personal author details and Git 
history, and use relative paths where possible. Cite sources normally; avoid wording that identifies 
you as an author of a cited source. Submission ownership is recorded through Learn, and staff use 
the final information page to identify the group. 
Optional supplementary code 
You may submit code as supplementary material. It can help staff and the assigned reviewer 
understand your implementation. Include a short README identifying the relevant files, 
dependencies and commands, and distinguish your changes from supplied code. 
Code is optional and is not a separate scoring category. The assessed argument and evidence must 
be available in the report and supporting video. Reviewers are not required to execute code. Submit 
source and small supporting files rather than model weights, full datasets, environments or caches. 
Exclude credentials and personal information.

3 
Individual review 
Each student reviews   one assigned submission individually . You will receive an anonymised 
written report and any accompanying supplementary code. You will not receive the video. 
Complete the four Learn text fields described in   the individual review guide : Summary, Strengths, 
Weaknesses and Detailed Comments. Your review is assessed for its quality. It does not determine 
the reviewed group's mark. 
Before submitting , make sure 
•   The PDF uses the supplied template and its main body is at most six pages. 
•   All technical content precedes the single final declaration/student - information page. 
•   The report, video and optional code follow the anonymity requirements. 
•   The video is at most ten minutes, contains a system demonstration and reserves its final two 
minutes for both released questions. 
•   Files open correctly and all intended materials are present in the Learn submission. 
The course team will provide rubric - based feedback on your group report and your individual review. 
The marking criteria are in   the group - report rubric   and   the individual - review rubric .
